messages:
tara: Heads-up: ran a cross-model baseline comparison for v3r vs v3q-int4 across our short-answer benchmark. Noting a small but consistent increase in hallucination rate on v3q-int4 for factual probes.

ian: by how much?

tara: about +3.1% absolute hallucination rate on a 6k sample. MRR drop was ~0.6%. Latency improved on average by 28ms p95.

samir: that's surprisingly high for short answers. Did you look at tokenization edge cases?

tara: yes, tokenization looks fine. More common in multi-step fact recall prompts. Might be quant noise in attention matrices.

sre-bot: note: if hallucination delta >3% we flag product and safety automatically per gatebook rule.

gatebook-bot: gatebook entry matched: "factual-hallucination-signal" -> escalate to safety team.

ian: escalate but don't block. Can we do a smaller staged rollout with extra reranker/validate?

tara: suggested mitigations: (1) add a lightweight post-rerank step for high-trust facts, (2) route high-fidelity customers to baseline for now, (3) instrument per-token attention variance to isolate layers.

samir: I'll spin up a focused quant-retrain with symmetric quantizer on attention weights and test int4v2.

tara: meanwhile I'll add a smoke test to e2e canary that checks a small set of high-precision factual probes and fails the gate if hallucination delta >1.5% on that slice.

ian: good. capture all this in a short runbook and we can re-evaluate after samir's quant pass.

release: archived snapshot. action items assigned.
